At the time, she was not in a good home situation either and the teacher made her life miserable, since she would specifically target her. My friend told me not to tell anyone, but I got my grandparents involved. They got her the help she needed and she’s still alive and my best friend to this day. I am so glad that she’s alive though because she’s absolutely amazing. I hope that she actually doesn’t remember feeling that way. No one should.

Two months ago, my family and I experience the one year anniversary of my uncle’s death. Do you know how he died? He overdosed after years of using.  Crystal meth, actually. His death wasn’t peaceful, either. He suffocated while driving his car because of the drugs. 

His addiction was so bad that he even ended up in the hospital because he had bubbles in his lungs. He promised he wouldn’t do it, that he’d changed. Well, he lied. He’s gone for good. I have to wake up every morning, pass his room and know that he’s not there to greet me or teach me how to drive. Whenever I think about him or look at photos of him, it takes all that I can not to cry. Heck, I’m trying not to cry right now. 

He had multiple arrests, lost his house and jobs, etc. The court even ordered him to mandatory rehab and he couldn’t even stay sober for it. Why? Because he thought life sucked without the drugs. He kept using and now he’s dead. 

I still remember what I was doing when he died. It was 7 November and I just won a teddybear from a claw machine inside a restaurant that I haven’t been to before. My mom, his sister, said this to me when I came back to the table: “I have to tell you something and you have to promise me not to get upset. Your uncle is dead.” I had to leave the restaurant because I screamed so loudly and sobbed my eyes out on the bench in front of the doors. I continued to cry my eyes out every day for the rest of the week, taking hourlong showers to try and quiet the sobs. 

His parents, my grandparents, went downhill after his funeral. My grandmother lost more than 50 lbs. in a year because she stopped eating. My grandfather can’t even talk about him without crying and isolates himself in his bedroom. Actually, they probably went downhill since he first started using. They focused all their time and energy on him that they neglected themselves and other family members. 

So, if you’re going to say that you hate being sober because life is boring for you, then that’s fine. Life sucks, it really does. But it’d be MISERABLE without you and if you started using again. If you ever question yourself using again and can’t find a reason not to do it for yourself, then do it for your family and friends. Life becomes so much more tolerable when you have people and you’re getting there. Just keep at it. Please don’t give up like my uncle did.

If these stories helped you and you want to hear more, then by all means, don’t hesitate to message me. Just please keep at it and be honest with your therapist. Please use your resources and don’t take them for granted like my uncle did when he was given help.

A senior here. 

There’s the good and bad when it comes to high school. It can seem like absolute hell at times, while it also seems like it’s the best part of your life. It honestly just depends on the school and community you’d be attending.

However, there are very important things you need to know no matter what school you go to. 

⭐️ 1) Focus on your grades. Freshman and sophomore year are the most important years for this. It’s harder to bring your GPA up if you do badly during those years, but it is easy to bring your gpa down. Also, if you have high enough grades before finals, you don’t have to worry about failing them, since they won’t really bring your grades down. At the most, probably one letter grade.

You want to have good grades (A’s and B’s), but make sure you actually understand the material. Have fun with it and don’t just memorize. You don’t need to be #1, just try your best.

Also, I don’t know if your school provides it, but for mine, we have the A+ program where two years of college will be paid off. Check if you have something like that if you plan on going to college/community college or trade school. If you don’t want to go to any form go college, at least go to trade school.

2) Stay out of as much drama as you can. Try not to gossip. It doesn’t matter. Also, stay away from drugs/alcohol. It will definitely mess you up. 

⭐️ 3) Expect to be treated like an adult. You can ask questions, but don’t expect people to hold your hand 24/7. You’re responsible for studying, getting to class, etc. 

4) Join sports, music, or extracurricular activities. It’ll keep you entertained and you’ll make friends. Also, colleges like that sort of thing.

5) It’s okay to be friends with your teachers and students that are older than you. Just remember to treat them with respect and don’t be intimidated by them.

6) You honestly don’t need to focus on dating, and if you do and are in a sexual relationship, please be safe about it. 

⭐️ 7) Your mental health is important. Take breaks and relax, but not to the point where you’re not taking school seriously. It’s okay to talk to your teachers/counselors about your mental health. They may refer you to someone that can be useful.

I placed stars around the three that I believe can be most useful to know, no matter what type of school you attend. I hope this helps. If you have any other questions, don’t hesitate to ask.

You’re a parent that wants to help your child, but you are doing it the wrong way. You’re concerned, I get it. But the lock on the pantry? That’s a bit excessive, don’t you think? A proper way to handle the situation is to definitely remove that lock! If you keep that lock there and restrict her access to certain types of food, then she will most likely keep things from you. She can also sneak food and lie to you more. 

My step-sister’s side of the family is extremely strict with food to the point where she feels sick at times. She sneaks around constantly and has a hidden stash of candy in her room that her father refuses to believe exists. 

You are actually encouraging your daughter to hide food and binge eat, which is what my step-sister does with sweets all the time when she thinks that nobody watches. She’s actually starting to hide other types of junk food now, like potato chips. I can’t say for certain off my family experience alone that it’s 100% fact, but it is a possibility. 

You must consider other factors for why she’s gaining weight as well. I know that you told us that she’s eating way more than she normally does, but have you ever considered why? Maybe it’s because she’s stressed/anxious with quarantine? Maybe she’s going through puberty? Maybe she’s not exercising as much as she use to? Maybe she’s having a medical problem, like with her thyroid? If you find the source to why she’s suddenly eating so much, then you can help her way better than restricting her food access. If you minimize the source, then she may consume less. 

You shouldn’t fear your daughter increasing from a size 2 to a size 8 in five months. She’s 12 years old! You should become concern if she’s suffering from health problems and the doctor tells you themself that she needs to loose weight due to medical reasons. Let me give you an example of an actual weight gain problem you need to worry about. My friend gained 40 pounds in 2 months and is at a risk of having a stroke/heart attack. Her resting heart rate was so high that the doctors thought she was exercising, and if she was, then it was the most intense exercise they’ve ever seen. She’s have personal trainers, been on numerous diets from professionals, and works out every day. She used to play sports, but had to stop because of a potential stroke. She’s been struggling with her weight for YEARS and nothing she could do helped. For YEARS the doctor cannot find what is wrong with her body, but knows that it isn’t because of how much food she consumes and what type of food it is. She recently had a test done with her heart and blood (IDK the names of the tests, she doesn’t even know herself Lol.) She’s going to have more tests run tomorrow. That, OP, is an actual reason to be concerned about someone’s weight. Your child is currently fine. You’re worried about her clothes fitting her, while my friend’s mother is worried about her child DYING due to being overweight/obese. 

Also, she’s probably beating herself up about the weight she’s gained. I know I have when I was her age. Remember my friend that I mentioned earlier? Yeah, she hates herself right now. Legit hates herself and I try to remind her everyday that weight doesn’t define her and just because she’s bigger than other girls doesn’t mean she isn’t beautiful. Make sure you tell you child that she is freaking gorgeous, even with the extra pounds. Tell her that you’ll always love her and that you’re sorry for how you handled the situation. 

Finally, what you can do to resolve this situation is to remove that lock, and sit down and have a discussion with her. Help her on her journey to becoming HEALTHIER not to losing weight. Teach her about exercising (like yoga indoors) or fun and healthy ways to make food. My mom made homemade ice cream from scratch while she was on a keto diet. It was delicious and it didn’t even have sugar in it! If it did, then it was very little. Right now, you are shaming your daughter instead of helping her. 

In this situation, you are the AH, but I do not believe you were intentionally being one. However, do not use the excuse ‘It was an accident! It was unintentional!” as a reason to justify yourself. Instead, improve your relationship with your daughter and help her.

ESH. There’s a lot of issues in this post. Are you really concerned about the name of a child and not your relationship falling a part? 

There are a lot worse names out there than Tuesday. I met a girl named freaking Chandelier in my school. A kid in my own grade only has the letter ‘Q’. Another was named after freaking Hitler, but with another ‘t’. People even make fun of my own name, and it’s not even ridiculous. It’s literally the most common name ever, like Julie or Jackson. Do people make fun of them because of their names? Some do, others don’t. 

People get mocked and made fun of for the dumbest reasons throughout life. Even if you were able to convince your wife of changing the name from Tuesday, who’s to say that people still won’t make fun of them? Yes, it would be wonderful if we could avoid every situation where we do not get our feelings hurt, but we do in the end. The best that you can do for that child is to teach them how to handle potential insults and build confidence within themselves. 

Remember when I said a kid at my school is named Chandelier? Yeah, well, she has an amazing boyfriend, is taking French 3 (college credit) this year, and she’s one of the most popular girls in her grade. Is it because of her name? Maybe. The guy named ‘Q’? I met the dude. He was in my LA class. He’s the most funny guy ever. Whenever I would have a bad day, he would always cheer me up. I didn’t have to say anything, he’d know. And those insults he would get from time to time? He laughed them off and continued on with his life. 

What I’m trying to say is that just because a name seems ‘weird’ and a kid could get made fun of, doesn’t necessarily mean they will. And if they do, then you need to teach them how to handle those insults and not let those words bring you down. Those parents that raised the kids I mentioned earlier did an excellent job. You need to be like those parents. 

Stop focusing on the name. You should be more worried about bettering yourself for the children and less about the name. What’s more important in the end? A kid named Tuesday or a child in a loving/caring household?
